subtype: Approach: never acting due to fear of rejection [Pitfall]
passage: Eshaan, since you ask what your Masi Ira was like at sixteen: scared. There was a boy in the next row, Vikram, who lent me his ruler in class nine, and I decided that was a sign. For months I rehearsed in the bathroom mirror. "Would you like to..." Every version had a hole in it. I wrote the sentence down and tore it up. Some days I got as far as his desk and asked about homework instead. Then one winter afternoon I saw Vikram walking to the library with Nalini, the two of them sharing one umbrella and laughing. I stood there holding my perfect sentence like a bag of stones. Vikram never knew. I can't say the answer would have been yes. But by never asking, I made sure of the no.

qa.q: What did Vikram lend Ira in class nine?
What was Ira feeling when Ira saw Vikram walking with Nalini?
qa.a: Ira felt crushed and full of regret, holding the perfect sentence 'like a bag of stones'.

qa.q: What could the young Ira have done instead of rehearsing for months, and why?
qa.a: Ira could have asked once, quietly and simply, accepting yes or no, because a real answer even a no is better than months of waiting.

qa.q: How might Vikram have seen Ira during those months?
qa.a: Vikram probably saw a classmate who sometimes asked about homework and had no idea of the feelings behind it, so there was never a question to answer.

grounding: The student rehearses endlessly and never speaks, and after months the crush starts talking with someone else, so avoiding a no also removes any chance of a yes.

subtype: Approach: never acting due to fear of rejection [Pitfall]
passage: Jatin had exactly one term to say something: Lavanya's family was moving to Pune in April. He knew because he had heard her tell a friend in October. Every Monday he promised himself: this week. He wrote the words in the back of his rough book: "Do you want to come to the robotics expo with a few of us?" He practised them in the bathroom mirror, on the walk to school, under his breath in maths. Each time she passed his desk, his throat closed. What if she laughs? What if everyone finds out? By January, Lavanya had started staying back after class with Nikhil from the debate team, laughing about something on his phone. Jatin watched from the doorway, the rough book in his bag. Nobody had said no to him. Nobody had said anything at all.

qa.q: When was Lavanya's family moving to Pune?
What was Jatin feeling each time Lavanya passed his desk?
qa.a: He felt afraid, his throat closing, worried she would laugh or everyone would find out.

qa.q: What small step could Jatin have taken back in October?
qa.a: Ask the simple group question once, accepting that a no would sting but would at least be an answer.

qa.q: How might Lavanya have seen Jatin during those months?
qa.a: Lavanya probably had no idea, since he never spoke, so from her side there was nothing to respond to.

grounding: Shows a student rehearsing for months but never asking, under time pressure, until the crush grows close to someone else.

subtype: Approach: never acting due to fear of rejection [Pitfall]
passage: For five months, in the Salt Lake tuition class where they sat two benches apart, Hrithik typed messages to Himani and deleted them. "Hey, want to study for the physics test together?" Delete. "Saw you at the book fair." Delete. He knew she hummed when solving numericals and chewed the end of her pen. He told himself he was waiting for the right moment. Really, he was waiting for a moment with no chance of a no. Then in March, Himani started sitting with a new boy from the other batch, sharing earphones at the break. Hrithik scrolled back through his drafts: fourteen unsent messages. He felt sick and oddly relieved at the same time. At least she never said no. But she never had the chance to say yes either.

qa.q: How many unsent messages were in Hrithik's drafts?
What mixed feelings did Hrithik have in March?
qa.a: He felt sick with regret and oddly relieved, spared a no but aware he had lost any chance of a yes.

qa.q: What could Hrithik have done differently?
qa.a: Send one of the simple study messages early on, accepting a possible no, instead of waiting for a moment with no risk.

qa.q: How might Himani have seen Hrithik all those months?
qa.a: Himani likely saw only a quiet classmate two benches away, with no sign he wanted to talk more.

grounding: Shows a student avoiding any risk of rejection for months, until the crush starts spending time with someone else.
